bo-distill.author: Apoorv Agnihotri & Nipun Batra

bo-gp-distill.author: Jochen Görtler, Rebecca Kehlbeck & Oliver Deussen

bo-gpml.author: Carl E. Rasmussen & Christopher K. I. Williams

idea-mnist.title: Training a model on MNIST

idea-quantum-ai.title: Quantum computing & AI

news-rnn-task-modularity.author: Yuhang Wu, Shikuang Deng, Kangrui Du, Marcelo G. Mattar, Dani S. Bassett, Huajin Tang, Gang Pan, Shi Gu
news-rnn-task-modularity.note: Nature Machine Intelligence, 28 Sept 2026. qai-preskill-nisq.note: The essay that named the 'NISQ' era: what noisy intermediate-scale devices can and cannot realistically do.

src-belcak-long-context.note: Later tokens cost up to 7x more to generate than early ones on frontier open-weight models. The authors outline semantic state space models (SSSMs) and question whether long-context models are needed at all.

src-cybenko-1989.author: George Cybenko
src-cybenko-1989.note: The rigorous version of Nielsen's chapter 4: finite sums Σ αⱼ σ(wⱼ·x + θⱼ) with any continuous sigmoidal σ are dense in C([0,1]ⁿ), so one hidden layer suffices. The proof argues by contradiction — Hahn–Banach and the Riesz representation theorem turn a non-dense span into a nonzero measure that annihilates every σ(w·x + θ), and a Fourier argument shows sigmoidal functions are 'discriminatory', so that measure must vanish; it proves existence only, with no bound on the number of units and nothing about learning.
src-cybenko-1989.prereq: Nielsen ch. 4 for the intuition; functional analysis — Hahn–Banach, the Riesz representation theorem (the dual of C(K) as signed measures); basic Fourier analysis
src-cybenko-1989.title: Approximation by superpositions of a sigmoidal function

It carries the subtleties the chapter skips — using the full net with halved weights at test time as an approximate model average, and the max-norm constraint on incoming weight vectors that makes large learning rates safe.
src-dropout-hinton-2012.prereq: feedforward networks, training with SGD, what overfitting is
src-dropout-hinton-2012.title: Improving neural networks by preventing co-adaptation of feature detectors

sug-orch-sep.title: Quantum Approaches to Consciousness (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)

sug-skills-for-llm-02.note: Goes past the rules to the design discipline behind them — single responsibility, interface versus implementation, the shared token budget, behavioural evaluation instead of deterministic tests — and gives a decision rule for when a skill is the wrong mechanism at all (versus a memory file, a slash command, a subagent, an MCP server or a hook), which the docs never state.

sug-universal-approximation-01.note: The other 1989 proof Nielsen cites, reached through the Stone–Weierstrass theorem instead of duality: one hidden layer with any squashing function approximates any Borel measurable function between finite-dimensional spaces to any accuracy, given enough hidden units — a wider class of functions than Cybenko's continuous ones.
sug-universal-approximation-01.prereq: Stone–Weierstrass theorem, measure theory (Borel measurable functions, convergence in measure); Cybenko 1989 first
sug-universal-approximation-01.title: Multilayer feedforward networks are universal approximators

sug-world-models-industrie-06.note: The JEPA approach (predicting in latent space rather than pixels), applied to robot planning.
sug-world-models-industrie-06.title: V-JEPA 2: Self-Supervised Video Models Enable Understanding, Prediction and Planning

tn-deeptree.author: Chang Nie, Junfang Chen, Yajie Chen
tn-deeptree.note: A scalability result rather than a compression one: a tree tensor network built from antisymmetric interaction modules captures 2^L-order multiplicative feature interactions with no activation functions, and reaches 82.4% top-1 on ImageNet-1k with 35.9M parameters. Evidence that TN architectures can now be trained at a scale where they used to fail.
tn-deeptree.prereq: tree tensor networks, standard vision benchmarks
tn-deeptree.title: Deep Tree Tensor Networks for Image Recognition

tn-lm-survey.author: Matvei Tarasov, Salman Ahmadi-Asl, André L. F. de Almeida, Andrzej Cichocki
tn-lm-survey.note: The current map of the field for language models: a seven-stage taxonomy from tokenisation to interpretability, plus a compression-realisation gap that separates parameters removed on paper from speedup actually obtained in a running system. Read it to decide which of the other papers deserve your time.
tn-lm-survey.prereq: transformer architecture, tensor decompositions (TT, Tucker, CP)
tn-lm-survey.title: Tensor Methods for Language Models: From Token Representation to Training, Adaptation, Compression, Inference, and Interpretability

tn-mpo-picogpt.author: Younes Javanmard, Tanmoy Pandit, Masoud Mardani
tn-mpo-picogpt.note: Every linear layer of a ~1M-parameter GPT-2-style model is replaced by an MPO module: 5 to 13x compression per transformer block, and at bond dimension 16 the model keeps 97.7% of baseline token accuracy with 191,872 parameters instead of 1,020,224. The authors state the limitation themselves: weights are reconstructed dense at inference, so no FLOP or memory saving is realised yet.
tn-mpo-picogpt.prereq: MPO and MPS, transformer blocks, PyTorch
tn-mpo-picogpt.title: Compressing Transformer Language Models via Matrix Product Operator Decomposition: A Case Study on PicoGPT

tn-novikov.author: Alexander Novikov, Dmitry Podoprikhin, Anton Osokin, Dmitry Vetrov
tn-novikov.note: The paper that turned a tensor network into a drop-in layer: a dense weight matrix is reshaped into a high-order tensor and kept in Tensor-Train format, compressing the fully-connected layers of a VGG-class network by orders of magnitude at almost unchanged accuracy. Every later TN-layer paper is a variation on this construction, which is why it is the one founding article to read first.
tn-novikov.prereq: SVD and low-rank approximation, backpropagation, fully-connected layers
tn-novikov.title: Tensorizing Neural Networks

tn-qi-review.author: Guillermo Valverde, Igor García Olaizola, Giannicola Scarpa, Alejandro Pozas-Kerstjens
tn-qi-review.note: Critical review of both uses of tensor networks, as standalone models and as a compression layer inside ordinary networks, across application domains. The verdict is the useful part: most compression and interpretability claims still lack large-scale empirical validation, so read it before believing any single-benchmark result.
tn-qi-review.title: Quantum-inspired tensor networks in machine learning models

tn-tensorization-orus.author: Safa Hamreras, Sukhbinder Singh, Román Orús
tn-tensorization-orus.note: Position paper that states the interpretability argument precisely: tensorising a layer creates bond indices, latent spaces a dense network simply does not have, whose structure can be followed across depth. Also the clearest account of how tensorisation differs from quantisation, pruning and distillation.
tn-tensorization-orus.prereq: TT and MPS decompositions, basic mechanistic-interpretability vocabulary
tn-tensorization-orus.title: Tensorization is a powerful but underexplored tool for compression and interpretability of neural networks

tn-tt-rss.author: José Ramón Pareja Monturiol, Alejandro Pozas-Kerstjens, David Pérez-García
tn-tt-rss.note: TT-RSS converts a trained network into a tensor train from black-box queries and sample points only, approximating the function rather than interpolating it. Two consequences: parameters that encode the training distribution are obfuscated, and the MPS form gives direct access to topological phases, a concrete interpretability handle.
tn-tt-rss.prereq: tensor-train sketching, MPS, basic privacy notions
tn-tt-rss.title: Tensorization of Neural Networks for Improved Privacy and Interpretability

tndl-cheng-ttn-2019.author: Song Cheng, Lei Wang, Tao Xiang, Pan Zhang
tndl-cheng-ttn-2019.note: Replaces the MPS Born machine by a binary tree tensor network that exploits 2-D image structure and avoids the exponentially decaying correlations of MPS, trained and sampled with GPU-friendly sweeping algorithms and reported to preserve pixel correlations better and reach higher log-likelihood than MPS on random patterns and binary MNIST.
tndl-cheng-ttn-2019.prereq: MPS Born machine (Han et al.), tree tensor networks with canonical form, negative log-likelihood training
tndl-cheng-ttn-2019.title: Tree tensor networks for generative modeling

tndl-cichocki-2016.author: Andrzej Cichocki, Namgil Lee, Ivan Oseledets, Anh-Huy Phan, Qibin Zhao, Danilo P. Mandic
tndl-cichocki-2016.note: A long survey that presents tensor networks with graphical notation and covers tensorization plus the Tucker and Tensor-Train decompositions and their generalisations as tools for super-compression against the curse of dimensionality.
tndl-cichocki-2016.prereq: Linear algebra incl. SVD, Kronecker and Khatri-Rao products; no prior tensor background assumed
tndl-cichocki-2016.title: Tensor Networks for Dimensionality Reduction and Large-scale Optimization: Part 1 Low-Rank Tensor Decompositions

tndl-cohen-2016.author: Nadav Cohen, Or Sharir, Amnon Shashua
tndl-cohen-2016.note: Proves an equivalence between convolutional arithmetic circuits and tensor factorisations (shallow networks are CP, deep networks are hierarchical Tucker) and shows that, outside a negligible set, functions of polynomial-size deep networks need exponential size in a shallow one.
tndl-cohen-2016.prereq: CP and hierarchical Tucker decompositions, matricization rank, basic measure theory, convolutional networks
tndl-cohen-2016.title: On the Expressive Power of Deep Learning: A Tensor Analysis

tndl-efthymiou-2019.author: Stavros Efthymiou, Jack Hidary, Stefan Leichenauer
tndl-efthymiou-2019.note: A short hands-on tutorial that encodes images into MPS form, contracts the network in an autodiff-friendly parallel way with the open-source TensorNetwork library, and reaches 98% on MNIST and 88% on Fashion-MNIST with one unchanged architecture and a more-than-10x GPU speed-up.
tndl-efthymiou-2019.prereq: MPS and tensor-diagram notation basics; Python with an autodiff framework
tndl-efthymiou-2019.title: TensorNetwork for Machine Learning

tndl-exp-machines-2016.author: Alexander Novikov, Mikhail Trofimov, Ivan Oseledets
tndl-exp-machines-2016.note: Presents a predictor over feature interactions of every order whose exponentially large weight tensor (up to 2^160 entries) is stored in Tensor-Train format and fitted by stochastic Riemannian optimisation, matching high-order factorisation machines on MovieLens 100K.
tndl-exp-machines-2016.prereq: Tensor-Train format; logistic regression and factorisation machines; Riemannian optimisation helpful but not required
tndl-exp-machines-2016.title: Exponential Machines

tndl-gao-mpo-2020.author: Ze-Feng Gao, Song Cheng, Rong-Qiang He, Z. Y. Xie, Hui-Hai Zhao, Zhong-Yi Lu, Tao Xiang
tndl-gao-mpo-2020.note: Replaces the linear layers of deep networks by matrix product operators and tests FC2, LeNet-5, VGG, ResNet and DenseNet on MNIST and CIFAR-10, reporting large parameter reductions with maintained or even improved accuracy.
tndl-gao-mpo-2020.prereq: TT/MPO (TT-matrix) format, SVD truncation, structure of fully-connected and convolutional layers
tndl-gao-mpo-2020.title: Compressing deep neural networks by matrix product operators

tndl-garipov-2016.author: Timur Garipov, Dmitry Podoprikhin, Alexander Novikov, Dmitry Vetrov
tndl-garipov-2016.note: Extends Tensor-Train compression from fully-connected to convolutional layers by reshaping the 4-D kernel into a higher-order tensor before factorising it, reaching 80x whole-network compression with a 1.1% accuracy drop on CIFAR-10.
tndl-garipov-2016.prereq: TT-layers (Novikov et al. 2015), convolution as matrix multiplication, tensor reshaping
tndl-garipov-2016.title: Ultimate tensorization: compressing convolutional and FC layers alike

tndl-glasser-2019.author: Ivan Glasser, Ryan Sweke, Nicola Pancotti, Jens Eisert, J. Ignacio Cirac
tndl-glasser-2019.note: Rigorously compares non-negative MPS (equivalent to hidden Markov models), Born machines and the newly introduced locally purified states as probabilistic models, proving that some factorisations need unboundedly more resources than others and that locally purified states are the most expressive.
tndl-glasser-2019.prereq: MPS/TT ranks, hidden Markov models, probabilistic graphical models, Born rule, non-negative rank
tndl-glasser-2019.title: Expressive power of tensor-network factorizations for probabilistic modeling

tndl-han-born-2018.author: Zhao-Yu Han, Jun Wang, Heng Fan, Lei Wang, Pan Zhang
tndl-han-born-2018.note: Introduces the MPS 'Born machine' for unsupervised learning, trained by a DMRG-like algorithm that adapts tensor dimensions during training and sampled directly, tested on Bars-and-Stripes, random binary patterns and MNIST and discussed against the Hopfield model, Boltzmann machines and GANs.
tndl-han-born-2018.prereq: MPS canonical form and two-site sweeps (Schollwöck), maximum-likelihood generative modelling, Born rule
tndl-han-born-2018.title: Unsupervised Generative Modeling Using Matrix Product States

tndl-levine-2018.author: Yoav Levine, David Yakira, Nadav Cohen, Amnon Shashua
tndl-levine-2018.note: Shows that deep convolutional arithmetic circuits are tensor networks, so entanglement measures tied to the min-cut of the network graph quantify the input correlations a network can model and give direct control of inductive bias through channel numbers.
tndl-levine-2018.prereq: Convolutional arithmetic circuits and hierarchical Tucker view (Cohen et al.), tensor-network diagrams, entanglement entropy and Schmidt rank
tndl-levine-2018.title: Deep Learning and Quantum Entanglement: Fundamental Connections with Implications to Network Design

tndl-liu-entanglement.author: Yuhan Liu, Wen-Jun Li, Xiao Zhang, Maciej Lewenstein, Gang Su, Shi-Ju Ran
tndl-liu-entanglement.note: Represents classifiers as many-qubit matrix product states, shows that single-site and bipartite entanglement in the represented images indicates how important different pixels are, and uses this to guide the MPS architecture, cutting the number of needed qubits (pixels) to under one tenth with little accuracy loss on MNIST.
tndl-liu-entanglement.prereq: MPS classifiers (Stoudenmire and Schwab), von Neumann entanglement entropy from the Schmidt decomposition
tndl-liu-entanglement.title: Entanglement-Based Feature Extraction by Tensor Network Machine Learning

tndl-ma-tensorized-transformer.author: Xindian Ma, Peng Zhang, Shuai Zhang, Nan Duan, Yuexian Hou, Ming Zhou, Dawei Song
tndl-ma-tensorized-transformer.note: Replaces multi-head attention with 'Multi-linear attention' built on Block-Term Tensor Decomposition and parameter sharing, which greatly reduces Transformer parameters while improving results on PTB, WikiText-103, One-Billion and WMT-2016 English-German.
tndl-ma-tensorized-transformer.prereq: Transformer self-attention, Tucker and Block-Term decompositions, mode-n tensor-matrix products
tndl-ma-tensorized-transformer.title: A Tensorized Transformer for Language Modeling

tndl-oseledets-tt-2011.author: Ivan V. Oseledets
tndl-oseledets-tt-2011.note: Defines the Tensor-Train format and gives the stable SVD-based TT-SVD construction with a quasi-optimal error bound (factor sqrt(d-1)), plus TT-rounding and basic arithmetic (addition, Hadamard product, matrix-by-vector product) carried out directly in TT form.
tndl-oseledets-tt-2011.prereq: SVD and low-rank approximation, tensor unfolding (reshaping) notation, QR factorisation
tndl-oseledets-tt-2011.title: Tensor-Train Decomposition

tndl-schollwock-2011.author: Ulrich Schollwöck
tndl-schollwock-2011.note: A long pedagogical review that rebuilds DMRG entirely in matrix-product-state language (canonical forms, SVD-based compression, MPOs, variational ground-state search, time evolution), with the MPS core in Sections 4-6.
tndl-schollwock-2011.prereq: SVD and Schmidt decomposition; basic quantum-mechanics notation (Hilbert space, spin chains)
tndl-schollwock-2011.title: The density-matrix renormalization group in the age of matrix product states

tndl-stoudenmire-2018.author: E. M. Stoudenmire
tndl-stoudenmire-2018.note: Builds layered tree tensor networks whose lower layers come from an unsupervised physics-style coarse-graining of the data and optimises only the top layer for classification, at cost linear in input dimension and training-set size, with strong MNIST and Fashion-MNIST results.
tndl-stoudenmire-2018.prereq: MPS classifiers (Stoudenmire and Schwab), tree tensor networks with isometric tensors, density matrices and eigendecomposition
tndl-stoudenmire-2018.title: Learning relevant features of data with multi-scale tensor networks

tndl-wang-survey-2023.author: Maolin Wang, Yu Pan, Zenglin Xu, Guangxi Li, Xiangli Yang, Danilo Mandic, Andrzej Cichocki
tndl-wang-survey-2023.note: A broad survey of 'tensorial neural networks' covering data-side uses (multi-source fusion, multimodal pooling, compression, multi-task training, quantum data) and integrations with CNNs, RNNs, GNNs, Transformers, LLMs and quantum neural networks, plus toolboxes and future directions.
tndl-wang-survey-2023.prereq: CP/Tucker/TT basics (Cichocki Part 1 or Oseledets) and familiarity with CNN, RNN and Transformer architectures
tndl-wang-survey-2023.title: Tensor Networks Meet Neural Networks: A Survey and Future Perspectives
